To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the creation of fiber damage in a fixed-batt saw cleaner can be reduced without affecting the removal of trash by using combinations of increased fiber moistures, reduced combing ratios, reduced batt densities, and reduced saw speeds.
the damage to cotton fiber in the lint cleaner was greatest at the feed bar to saw interface, particularly when the combing ratio and saw speed were highest.
lint cleaner damage is reduced by increasing fiber moisture, lowering the saw speed, and reducing the combing ratio and batt density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of lint cleaners on the quality of the fibers they produce.
the effect of lint cleaning and fiber moisture on the fiber quality of cottons of differing length.
the design and operation of a fixed-batt saw type lint cleaner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the more aggressive settings for the lint cleaner resulted in a greater amount of fiber damage.
the most effective lint cleaner settings are the slowest feed roller speed and saw surface speed, lowest grid bar pressure, lowest combing ratio and batt density, and highest fiber moisture content.
the damage to the cotton fibers is reduced when the moisture content is increased, when the batt density is reduced, when the combing ratio is reduced, and when the saw speed is reduced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a more aggressive saw setting, i.e., a high saw speed, a high combing ratio, or a high batt density, is likely to result in a cleaner, but a more damaged fiber, and a less aggressive setting is likely to result a cleaner, but more contaminated, fiber.
the use of a more aggressive lint cleaner can be justified only if the fiber damage is not excessive.
the damage to cotton fiber quality by lint cleaners can be reduced by employing combinations of reduced fiber moisture, lower saw speed, reduced combing ratios, and reduced batt densities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of lint cleaners should consider the effect of the settings on the cotton being processed.
it is possible to reduce fiber damage in the fixed-batt saw cleaner without increasing trash content.
the saw speed, combing ratio, batt density, fiber length, and fiber moisture content are all important parameters in the design and operation of fixed-batt saw cleaners.
